item.title: Go Daily Question 128
item.description:
Will the following code compile? If so, what will be the output?

func GetValue() int {
 return 1
}

func main() {
 i := GetValue()
 switch i.(type) {
 case int:
 println("int")
 case string:
 println("string")
 case interface{}:
 println("interface")
 default:
 println("unknown")
 }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Compilation fails. i.(type) The syntax for type assertion is i.(type), where i is an interface and type is a fixed keyword. It’s important to note that only interface types can use type assertion. Official: https://go.dev/tour/methods/16

item.title: Go Daily Question 067
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type A interface {
 ShowA() int
}

type B interface {
 ShowB() int
}

type Work struct {
 i int
}

func (w Work) ShowA() int {
 return w.i + 10
}

func (w Work) ShowB() int {
 return w.i + 20
}

func main() {
 c := Work{3}
 var a A = c
 var b B = c
 fmt.Println(a.ShowB())
 fmt.Println(b.ShowA())
}

A. 23 13 B. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

B Key takeaway: Static type of interfaces. a and b have the same dynamic type and dynamic value, which are Work struct and {3} respectively. The static type of a is A, and the static type of b is B. Interface A does not include method ShowB(), and interface B does not include method ShowA(), resulting in a compilation error.

item.title: Go Daily Question 047
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {
 a := [2]int{5, 6}
 b := [3]int{5, 6}
 if a == b {
 fmt.Println("equal")
 } else {
 fmt.Println("not equal")
 }
}

A. compilation error B. equal C. not equal

🔑 Answer Analysis:

A Only arrays of the same capacity and same type can be compared.
